co_wolfmother_s.blurb: Wolfmother's is a small trad wall on Mother's Buttress in Unaweep Canyon, in the Grand Junction area. The eleven routes here are mostly 5.10 and 5.11 lines, with a single 5.9 and one 5.12, and several run to multiple pitches, so expect a real day out rather than a quick lap. The stone is highly featured and rewards face climbing. In warm months the wall holds shade until late morning, while winter brings sun from mid-morning onward. Route-finding can be easy to get wrong and loose blocks remain between established lines, so move carefully and bring a helmet.

co_rib_rock_north_lower_rib_cage.blurb: The Rib Cage is the steep lower section of Rib Rock's north face in the Estes Park Valley. All eleven routes are bolted sport lines, weighted heavily toward 5.12, with a few 5.11s and one each at 5.10 and 5.13, so it suits strong climbers looking for sustained, overhanging terrain. The wall faces north and stays shady, which makes it a pleasant choice on hot days. Reaching it means following a forest trail and then scrambling up talus to the base. Wear a helmet, since loose material can fall from above.

co_ridgway_dike_wall.blurb: Ridgway Dike Wall is a short roadside sport crag a few miles south of Ridgway on the way toward Ouray. Its eleven bolted routes run from about 5.7 to 5.11, with the bulk sitting around 5.9 and 5.10, making it a handy stop for moderate climbers. The tallest faces reach roughly ninety feet. Most lines face east, so they catch morning light and otherwise stay cool, even in midsummer. Holds can be loose, so test them, stay on the bolted lines, and wear a helmet, especially while belaying.

co_sunset_cliff.blurb: Sunset Cliff is one of the crags above Lincoln Creek, off Highway 82 on the Aspen side of Independence Pass. It holds eleven routes, mostly trad with a couple of sport lines, spanning from an approachable 5.8 crack up to 5.13 at the top end. The middle of the range, around 5.10 and 5.11, is where most of the climbing sits. The cliff stays shaded in the morning until about two in the afternoon, which makes it a good summer morning choice. Reaching the base means a walk along the river and then up through the woods.

co_tiger_wall.blurb: Tiger Wall sits in Hartman Rocks, west of Gunnison, and is easy to pick out near the road thanks to the striped look of its granite. Ten of the eleven routes are bolted sport climbs, with one trad line. The grades lean hard: mostly 5.12, a handful of 5.11s, and singles at 5.10 and 5.13. The climbing is steep and slabby, and the wall faces west. The routes can't be reached from the top of the cliff, so plan on leading and lowering from below.

co_upper_wall_3.blurb: The Upper Wall is a small cliff high on the hillside above Real Hidden Valley in Clear Creek Canyon near Golden. Walls here stand about thirty to forty feet. Ten of the eleven routes are trad, with one top-rope line, and some mixed bolted-and-gear lines are also described. Difficulty ranges from an easy 5.6 through the 5.7 and 5.8 range, a cluster of 5.10s, and one 5.12 at the top. Expect a steady uphill walk to reach it, and keep in mind that the short routes make it a quiet spot for a few laps.
co_upper_wall_3.approach: Continue up the slope above the foot of the Real Hidden Valley crag. Stay slightly west at first, then angle back east to avoid a steeper section. The wall is roughly 10 to 15 minutes above.
